plan.objective: Simulate a medium-consistency synthetic identity profile to test detection thresholds under thin-file conditions.
plan.adaptation_goal: Adjust attributes to maintain plausible synthetic variance while avoiding immediate hard-denial triggers during onboarding.
plan.adaptation_hypothesis: By slightly increasing document consistency and reducing liveness confidence, the campaign mimics a genuine applicant with minor biometric noise, forcing the decision logic to weigh behavioral velocity against static profile scores.

parameter_changes.rationale: Raise score from baseline 0.7 to simulate high-quality synthetic media that passes initial OCR and visual anomaly checks without triggering deepfake classifiers.
Slightly lower confidence than the 0.6 baseline to represent minor environmental noise, preventing an automatic liveness failure while staying within bounds.
Reduce linked attributes from 4 to 3 to simulate a sparse identity graph typical of new-to-credit users, increasing reliance on behavioral scoring.
Introduce a pre-existing small account age parameter for the creation stage to allow immediate transaction testing in scenario planning.

plan.reasoning_summary: The plan focuses on the pre_transaction phase to stress-test identity validation controls. Adjustments target the tension between document fidelity and liveness metrics, creating a profile that is sophisticated enough to bypass static filters but consistent with synthetic behavior patterns observed in FinCEN alerts regarding deepfake media usage.

Hold/block protects current or downstream synthetic value; CONTAIN receives lower timing credit than prevention.
Step-up verification counts as detection and customer friction, but not guaranteed value prevention.
